stem: Solve the inequality: 3x - 7 > 2x + 1. Which of the following describes all solutions?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student moves 7 to the right side with the wrong sign: 3x - 2x > 1 - 7 = -6, misreading the direction of transposition.
Student solves correctly to x > 8 but reverses the inequality sign, writing x < 8.
Student subtracts 2 from both sides instead of collecting x terms: 3x - 7 > 2x + 1 becomes x - 7 > 1, then x > 8; or makes arithmetic error giving x > 6.

explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 7 > 1. Add 7 to both sides: x > 8.

explanation_sections.punchline: Collecting x terms gives x > 1 + 7, which is x > 8. Moving terms across the inequality sign changes their sign, not the direction of the inequality.
explanation_sections.approach: Linear inequality problems are solved exactly like linear equations, with one rule added: if you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the inequality sign. Here all operations are addition and subtraction, so the sign stays the same. Collect all x terms on one side, all constants on the other.
explanation_sections.lesson: The inequality direction flips only when you multiply or divide by a negative number. Adding or subtracting on both sides never changes the direction.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Two steps: subtract 2x, then add 7. Eliminate option x < 8 in five seconds: the inequality direction is wrong.
